expert_skill.cornering: At least 5/6 clean; braking before turn-in; intended exit; no rescue; final two equal first two.
expert_skill.jump_scrub: At least 5/6 clean on two days with matched entry speed, lower trajectory and unchanged landing/exit quality.

promotion_logic.deload: Use for dated taper/consolidation, repeated abnormal next-day response, repeated technical degradation, density breach, impaired/compromised CNS, or persistent/focal/asymmetric/mechanics-altering symptoms.
promotion_logic.hold: Use when response is pending, review fields are incomplete, a trigger was obeyed, or a technical dimension exceeds its fatigue/error ceiling.
promotion_logic.one_lever_rule: Progress only one of frequency, duration, engine dose, complete-cycle count, technical consequence or strength at a time.
promotion_logic.promote: Only after the written rung is executed inside its stop, form, technical and next-day absorption gates.
promotion_logic.unsafe_override: A triggered_but_continued outcome never promotes the nominal rung; retain delivered-action, execution-boundary and safety-adherence learning separately.

adaptive_programming.purpose: Turn persistent Garmin evidence, structured athlete feedback, canonical strategy and the dated roadmap into an inspectable training direction, progression rung, weekly role budget and promotion/hold decision.

It cannot override same-day safety constraints.
artifact_contract.cns_readiness: snapshots/cns_readiness.json is the current technical-consequence ceiling after current_state rebuild.
artifact_contract.coaching_architecture: config/coaching_architecture.json is the durable training architecture for future agents.

do_not_assume: Do not confuse historical 222 W P20 with the current Garmin operational FTP; use the latest dated Garmin FTP surface with its clean-test-validity caveat.
Do not count elliptical load as bike-specific maintenance.
Do not treat Garmin readiness as direct trail-skill readiness without subjective notes.
Do not infer exercise-time oxygenation or respiration from daily or sleep Garmin summaries.
Do not treat a displayed AQI or PM2.5 concentration as readiness clearance, and do not conflate AQI with concentration units.
Do not treat low training load as permission for high-consequence MTB when CNS readiness is impaired or compromised.
Do not use historical finger injury as a current training gate.
Do not copy a full ideal week when life load, sleep, HRV, arm pump, or back-to-back trail plans require density control.
individual_response: Bike-specific load and frequency are Clayton's main durable fitness currency.
Total load can be a false signal when elliptical, run, or gym replaces bike work.
Structured bike tempo/threshold improves sustained power, but must be recoverable and placed away from key trail days.
High MTB months can build durability while hiding P20 if there is no clean power expression.
Gym supports durability only when it does not steal trail quality.
Directive macro standards help only when the daily Garmin/readiness layer prevents them from becoming unabsorbed density.
CNS readiness is separate from physical readiness; Body Battery rebound does not prove visual processing, decision speed, braking timing, or technical confidence are restored.

normal_training.density_rule: An Enduro training exposure replaces a protected MTB slot rather than stacking as an extra costly day. Official practice and racing on a declared event weekend are modeled as event exposures, not extra training touches, and require taper plus post-event recovery.
scope: race-bike chassis, braking, impact and cockpit validation

caveats: This architecture is observational and personal to Clayton's Garmin record.
P20 is an observed expression metric; trail-heavy months can build real enduro fitness without a clean P20.
Modern HRV/wake Body Battery is strongest from March 2026 onward.
Subjective trail notes are required for expert-skill decisions.

cycling_vo2_rebuild.conference_week_2026_W35: If Monday is absorbed cleanly, Wednesday becomes 3x8 minutes of controlled tempo/torque at 165-170 W rather than another recovery-only session; Tuesday and Thursday remain low-cost touches and Friday remains the sole Enduro training exposure.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.dose_progression_rule: Treat 60 minutes at 120-130 W as the normal low-cost continuity anchor. Build one weekly duration exposure toward 75-90 minutes near 125 W and use exactly one structured engine exposure such as tempo/torque, VO2 intervals or the 60-minute 145 W benchmark. Do not stack all three structured variants in one week.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.initial_post_conference_weekly_bike_load: Approximately 400-500 Garmin bike load as a secondary audit range, not a quota. Unique bike days, meaningful-cost count, absorption and technical-final-run quality remain primary.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.interpretation: The gap is partly genuine deconditioning and partly relative-mass and Garmin-observability effects. At current mass, unchanged historical absolute oxygen-use proxy would read about 49.8; the remaining gap is consistent with lower chronic bike load and reduced sustained aerobic continuity. MTB stochastic power, powerless Enduro rides and heat can reduce clean Garmin cycling-VO2 observation.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.post_conference_progression: Introduce one true VO2 session per week starting with 4x3 minutes at 225-235 W with 3 minutes easy, then progress to 5x3 before increasing interval duration. Keep only three weekly meaningful costs and protect Enduro or Denai course quality.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.recurring_build_rule: Use 5-6 unique bike days when recovery and calendar allow: 2-3 meaningful sessions including one structured aerobic-development stimulus, 2 protected MTB exposures and 2-3 low-cost continuity or primer touches. Do not make two key rides plus three recovery-only rides the recurring VO2 rebuild template.
validation: Standardized power-to-HR response and decoupling under comparable Suito cooling and fueling.
VO2-rep power spread, cadence preservation and final RPE.
Comparable Twin Peaks climbing power and RPE drift.
Final-descent vision, braking precision, front tracking and arm-pump equality versus the first descent.
Garmin cycling VO2 trend over 4-6 weeks as a secondary outcome, not the sole target.
cycling_vo2_rebuild.weight_rule: Do not aggressively cut body mass before PDR26; fuel training and use post-race body-composition work only if it preserves power, recovery and technical quality.

decision_hierarchy: Sabbath hard rest and current readiness.
CNS readiness: cap technical consequence, novelty, speed, jumps, enduro simulation, and setup testing when nervous-system processing is not restored.
Garmin freshness: wellness, activity, and training status must be current for hard guidance; Garmin Training Readiness is separately dated context only.

Same-day environment: before a weather- or haze-sensitive outdoor call, inspect the current IQAir TTDI weather and air-quality report directly and combine it with symptoms, trail conditions, duration and ventilation; this is transient coaching context, not a persistent software gate.
Garmin diagnosis arbitration: use Training Status, ACWR, and Load Focus to decide whether the session ceiling should downshift, hold, or allow a controlled upgrade.
Current phase and recent load: avoid spikes while rebuilding.
Bike-specific continuity: protect the weekly minimum before adding non-bike work.
MTB specificity: protect trail quality and durability exposures before gym or extra intensity.
Power prescription: use the current dated Garmin operational FTP plus RPE/HR validation; historical P20 is not FTP.
Nutrition and heat: fuel technical quality before late-session skill degradation appears.

clipless_adaptation.athlete_response: Clipless felt natural on the Enduro and possibly slightly more comfortable than flat pedals.
clipless_adaptation.coaching_interpretation: The primary adaptation is transfer of clipless automaticity and dynamically centred rider behavior from the Stumpjumper to the Enduro. Foot security is a secondary enabler of front-tyre authority and bike-body separation, not evidence that the pedals alone created the technical improvement.
clipless_adaptation.comparison_context: The prior 2026-06-12 Enduro exposure used flat pedals; the 2026-08-08 re-entry followed a 57-day Enduro-specific gap while clipless skill had been developed on the Stumpjumper.
clipless_adaptation.validation_constraint: Keep the pedal system fixed during the next matched Enduro repeat. Retain clipless as successful Enduro transfer only while release remains automatic, knee and hip response stay clean, centred posture and front tracking persist, and the rider does not rely on pulling against the pedals to correct the bike.

rear_shock_setups.comparison_rule: The custom damper tuning makes the complete chassis responses closely matched and the athlete has validated immediate interchangeability, while the air and coil springs retain subtle terrain-specific differences. Do not demand a new equivalence proof after every swap; use a course-specific shakedown to confirm installation, pressure or preload, clicks, tyre pressures and current rider response.

latest_validation.positive_evidence: No wallow, low-ride-height control problem, bottom-out, pack-down, rear kick, pitch, missed line, reactive brake, correction, rescue or near miss. Mid-stroke support was good and vision/decision speed was 9/10.
latest_validation.rider_constraint: A little Flintstone arm pump was associated with rough rock gardens and less-relaxed hands; treat rider relaxation as primary until matched evidence implicates the chassis.
latest_validation.route_context: Mixed-intent Pure Quill plus 65-percent Flintstone re-entry after about one year away, with long friend waits. This was a current-state air-shock revalidation, not a new matched air-versus-coil comparison.
latest_validation.unresolved_evidence: Unloaded rear grip felt lower and seated ride height felt slightly lower than the coil. Very dry trail, rider loading, unknown token count and unverified sag remain confounders. Exact O-ring travel and pedal-strike outcome were not reported.

rear_shock_setups.next_test: For the next race selection, keep the chosen shock fixed and complete a course-representative shakedown. Record full-kit sag or coil preload, O-ring travel where applicable, unloaded-rear tracking, pedal strikes, arm pump and final-stage precision. Change the choice only for a repeated course-relevant symptom, not a single dry-trail sensation.

prior_back_to_back_validation.confidence: High for athlete-specific functional interchangeability and race-option status; moderate for generalizing either terrain advantage beyond the tested contexts.
prior_back_to_back_validation.evidence_scope: Athlete-confirmed riding validation. The exact comparison date, route, run-level telemetry and any damper dyno sheet are not currently preserved.
prior_back_to_back_validation.method: Athlete-confirmed direct back-to-back testing of the custom-tuned air and coil shocks on the same Enduro platform.
prior_back_to_back_validation.result: Differences were subtle enough that Clayton could swap between the two without a meaningful reacclimation period. The coil produced the preferred response and speed on DH lines; the air shock produced subtly better pumping support.

race_selection.air_preference: Pumpy, pedally or compression-rich stages where rider-generated speed, platform support and the lower system weight are useful.
race_selection.coil_preference: Faster, rougher or longer DH-biased stages where repeated impacts, braking bumps and rear tracking are decisive.
race_selection.mixed_course_rule: Choose the shock whose subtle advantage applies to the race's most decisive stages; do not choose from weight alone. Complete a course-specific shakedown after installation while retaining the recorded shock and tyre settings.

rear_shock_setups.working_status: Both the Super Deluxe Ultimate Air and Super Deluxe Coil Ultimate are athlete-validated, immediately swappable race options. Prior back-to-back testing established closely matched overall chassis behavior, and the 2026-08-18 ride successfully revalidated the air setup under the current clipless riding context.

training_use_policy.density_rule: An Enduro training exposure replaces a protected MTB slot rather than stacking as an extra costly day. Official practice and racing on a declared event weekend are modeled as event exposures, not extra training touches, and require taper plus post-event recovery.

specialized_stumpjumper.default_role: Primary outdoor fitness and volume MTB training bike with current power meter.
specialized_stumpjumper.mileage_policy: Clayton is comfortable putting training mileage on the Stumpjumper.
specialized_stumpjumper.preferred_training_use: Routine MTB engine work, climbing repeatability, durability volume and appropriate technical training. Use the power meter for comparable climb work and control descent intent when the physiological target is primary.

setup_history.change: Fork rebound damping increased by one click and shock rebound damping reduced by one click.
setup_history.rider_rationale: The fork rebound increase addressed front-wheel ping over big hits that had pushed Clayton rearward; treat the slower rebound as a previously successful correction rather than an untested cause.

setup_history.change: Fork HSC one click firmer than the 2026-07-28 setting.
setup_history.interpretation: Treat HSC as a provisional intent- and readiness-dependent setting: firmer attack support when fresh versus the softer compliance setting for genuinely chill riding. Validate rather than assuming either setting is universally superior.
setup_history.negative_context: During a separate illness-fatigue period Clayton could not ride the firmer setting effectively and returned HSC one click softer.
setup_history.positive_context: Clayton previously loved this setting at maximum attack on 2K+ through successive hits.

setup_history.change: Tested the fork one click firmer in HSC than the 2026-07-28 setting while retaining the previously successful slower rebound direction.
setup_history.interpretation: Retain HSC +1 provisionally as the attack setting. The primary gain is improved rider centring and front-pressure authority; the firmer HSC is a credible secondary enabler by holding the front higher under larger impacts. Do not credit the result to setup alone and do not add another click.
setup_history.objective_context: At the 1,118.38 m distance-synchronised overlap, the 2K lap was 11.768 seconds (5.5 percent) faster than 2026-07-25 and 7.551 seconds (3.6 percent) faster than 2026-07-28, with no lap-comparator quality flags. Power was also higher, so this is not a setup-only gain. Pure Quill was shortened by a missed exit and did not reproduce the prior 38 km/h maximum-speed condition.
setup_history.rider_outcome: Clayton reported a stronger dynamically centred posture, greater willingness to load the front, no leftward veer, no perceived rear wallow, more controlled corner exits, and remaining chassis headroom.
setup_history.validation_constraint: Re-test HSC +1 on an exact familiar route at 85-90 percent with no other setup changes. Keep it only if the fork recovers between successive hits without ping, pack-down, harsh deflection, left pull, rearward hip retreat, rear wallow, kick, chassis pitch, loss of small-hit grip, or increased hand and braking fatigue.

setup_history.change: Promoted fork HSC +1 relative to the 2026-07-28 setting from provisional attack setting to the working Stumpjumper baseline for normal-readiness, familiar Bukit Kiara riding.
setup_history.interpretation: The primary adaptation remains Clayton's dynamically centred posture, deliberate front loading and rapid recentering. HSC +1 is a secondary enabler that plausibly preserves chassis support so that rider skill can be expressed. HSC responds to damper shaft speed rather than trail speed, so a harsher feel at slower pace is acceptable only while tyre tracking, grip and hand/upper-body fatigue remain clean. Do not add another click or use HSC -1 as a workaround for declining focus.
setup_history.rider_outcome: In a chill-pace within-ride HSC +1 / HSC -1 / HSC +1 sequence, Clayton reported that +1 felt harsher but retained greater exit commitment; -1 produced more mid-turn braking and reduced commitment to the exit. Returning to +1 on a partial final 2K confirmed the preferred control direction before focus declined.
setup_history.scope: Working baseline only for normal-readiness, familiar Kiara terrain. Wet roots, long rough descents, unfamiliar terrain and impaired or compromised CNS readiness remain unvalidated; impaired or compromised CNS status blocks technical testing rather than selecting a softer setting to continue.
setup_history.validation_constraint: Hold tyre pressures, fork air/sag, rebound, shock and other setup variables constant. Falsify HSC +1 if matched runs show front ping, skip, harsh lateral deflection, reduced root or small-hit grip, travel starvation, pack-down, rear kick, chassis pitch, rearward hip retreat, left pull, reactive braking, missed exits or greater hand, braking or upper-body fatigue.

fueling_architecture.heat_rule: In Kuala Lumpur, treat fuel/hydration as skill protection: sloppy braking, weak pumping, timid jumps, or poor line choice late can be carb/sodium/heat failure.
fueling_architecture.range_selection_rule: Choose within the canonical band from same-day heat/humidity, actual sweat response, session consequence, and gut tolerance. Previous-session weather is not a forecast, and Garmin heat acclimation never reduces the target by itself.

cns_readiness_model.decision_role: Use CNS readiness as a technical-consequence ceiling after Sabbath and physical readiness, not as a replacement for Garmin readiness.
inputs: Subjective CNS notes: brain fog, vision narrowing, delayed line choice, braking timing, unclipping delay, motivation, and confidence.
Garmin wellness context: HRV status, overnight HRV versus baseline, resting HR, stress, sleep score, wake Body Battery, and current Body Battery.
Wear-state coverage: material internal Garmin gaps withhold positive low-stress credit; the gap itself is not fatigue or recovery evidence, while high observed stress may still lower the ceiling.
Completed rest-window cognition: poor post-rest clarity, prolonged sleep inertia, and structured illness may lower the CNS ceiling; positive stress or Body Battery response cannot raise it.
Post-activity self-evaluation: weak or very weak feel, especially when RPE is low.
Recent MTB neural cost: long technical duration, meaningful trail load, high-HR trail minutes, and back-to-back technical exposure, carried into the following 48 hours with declining weight.
non_overrides: CNS readiness cannot authorize intensity when physical readiness is red.
Good Body Battery cannot override brain fog, strained HRV, weak feel, or delayed decision speed.
Low load cannot justify technical consequence if CNS status is impaired or compromised.
cns_readiness_model.purpose: Estimate whether Clayton's nervous system can safely process speed, line choice, braking timing, jumps, setup tests, and technical consequence.

status_meaning.compromised: Use recovery or low-consequence repetition only; no speed hunting, jump progression, race simulation, or setup testing.
status_meaning.impaired: Recovery only for training purposes; no MTB quality, intervals, gym loading, or high-consequence technical work.
status_meaning.ready: No independent CNS cap; physical readiness, route consequence, and session contract still govern.
status_meaning.watch: Skill practice can proceed only if narrow, familiar, and low-to-moderate consequence.

trail_specific_field_gate.chill_rule: Chill reduces speed, physiological load and consequence, not attentional engagement. If Clayton cannot maintain deliberate visual processing at chill pace, stop technical work rather than using a setup change or extra confirmation lap to continue.
trail_specific_field_gate.fail_action: A surprise deflection, delayed or missed line, reactive mid-turn braking, narrowed visual horizon, declining focus, or unusually high compensatory attention removes further setup attribution and optional descents; use the safest familiar egress.
trail_specific_field_gate.interpretation_rule: A later clean run achieved through materially greater conscious focus may show that the bike setup is usable, but it does not prove normal CNS reserve or erase an earlier rider-error event.
trail_specific_field_gate.purpose: A clean car-park or low-speed opening gate cannot by itself prove trail-speed visual processing, decision timing or steering precision. Treat the first familiar low-consequence climb and technical segment as a second diagnostic gate before granting repeats.
sequence: Run the written low-speed opening gate for gross coordination, steering symmetry, bike-body separation and obvious physical or CNS impairment.

Compare the first deliberately easy climb with its written RPE ceiling. Disproportionate RPE or unexpectedly effortful execution removes optional technical volume even when the opening gate was clean.

On the first familiar low-consequence trail segment, check visual horizon, line-choice latency, braking timing, intentional front tracking and whether normal execution feels automatic or requires unusually deliberate compensatory focus.

integrated_coaching_model.coaching_standard: More is not better; more specific, better absorbed, and more repeatable is better.

allowed_outputs.controlled_upgrade: When Garmin status is Productive or Peaking, ACWR is optimal, readiness is not red, CNS is not compromised, and load focus shows the objective needs more specific stimulus, the coach may raise an easy plan into a bounded high-aerobic or MTB repeatability session.
allowed_outputs.downshift: When ACWR is non-optimal, Garmin status is Recovery/Unproductive/Overreaching/Strained, readiness is red, CNS readiness is impaired/compromised, or the session would stack the wrong load bucket, reduce the ceiling.
allowed_outputs.hold_plan: When Garmin status supports the written plan but does not clearly expose a useful stimulus gap, follow the plan and protect the next key session.
allowed_outputs.no_hard_guidance: When Garmin freshness is limited, do not use stale status to justify intensity.

inputs: Training Status feedback such as Productive, Maintaining, Recovery, Unproductive, Overreaching, or Strained.
Garmin acute/chronic workload ratio and status.
Load Focus buckets for low aerobic, high aerobic, and anaerobic relative to Garmin target ranges.
Freshness of wellness, activity, and training-status data.
Clayton's subjective sharpness and technical intent.
load_focus_rules: If low aerobic is above target while high aerobic is below or inside target, do not keep adding only easy volume; consider controlled tempo, torque, or MTB repeatability if readiness, CNS readiness, and route consequence agree.
If anaerobic is near or above its upper target, avoid stacking sprints, VO2, or full-attack descents even when Productive.
If high aerobic is low and anaerobic is not near the upper target, a controlled high-aerobic session can be more useful than another recovery ride.
Garmin can raise the stimulus ceiling only within an explicit contract; it cannot authorize open-ended mission creep.
non_overrides: Red readiness or hard-session avoid guidance.
Poor subjective sharpness, unsafe trail conditions, or technical consequence above the session purpose.
garmin_diagnosis_arbitration.purpose: Use Garmin's sport-specific diagnosis as a structured co-diagnostic signal while keeping the coach responsible for MTB-specific execution, route consequence, and adaptation logic.

garmin_surface_governance.decision_boundary: A non-empty Garmin response is not automatically usable evidence. Validate the required nested surface, keep latest-attempt state separate from last-known-good data, and reduce confidence rather than inferring absence.
garmin_surface_governance.device_metadata_rule: Devices & Apps is usable only when the activity response contains valid device metadata. Missing metadataDTO is unknown, not evidence of wrist HR.
garmin_surface_governance.device_readiness_capability_rule: Training Readiness capability is false only after a successful non-empty device response explicitly reports false for the registered devices; failed, empty, or capability-absent responses remain unknown.
garmin_surface_governance.latest_session_rule: Use the compact latest-session block to interpret what load represented, but respect HR-source confidence, weather-unit gates, Garmin modeled-water limits, loop-estimation limits, and stale-power policy.
garmin_surface_governance.moving_duration_rule: For steep hiking, preserve Garmin movingDuration as raw and withhold stopped-time subtraction when timer and elapsed duration agree but reported moving time is physiologically or mechanically implausible.
garmin_surface_governance.oxygenation_rule: Keep daily, sleep, and activity-time Pulse Ox and respiration separate. Negative activity-period sentinels mean unavailable, not normal; absent activity samples cannot be inferred from sleep values, and wrist Pulse Ox cannot promote readiness or establish medical safety.
garmin_surface_governance.readiness_rule: Reject wrong-date Training Readiness rows, expose source date and age, and keep the feed context-only behind Sabbath, physical readiness, CNS ceiling, and freshness constraints.
garmin_surface_governance.surface_manifest: Use snapshots/garmin_surface_manifest.json to distinguish configured, collected, normalized, consumed, empty, failed, unsupported, and never-attempted Garmin surfaces.

operating_loop: Diagnose the current limiter from Garmin history plus recent subjective trail evidence.
Choose the highest-specificity session that fits the week and recovery state.

Resolve session provenance: explicit coach-authored plan overrides matching weekly intent, but Sabbath, physical readiness, data freshness, Garmin arbitration, and CNS ceilings can still replace or cap either source.
Prescribe purpose, dose, adaptation hypothesis, execution rules, expected result, and stop rules.
After sync, compare expected versus actual load, CNS readiness, self-evaluation, skill notes, and next-day response.
Update the next prescription and the athlete model only when the evidence changes the coaching call.
integrated_coaching_model.purpose: Combine directive enduro-specific coaching with Garmin-backed N-of-1 verification.

same_day_environment_context.access_rule: Read the current report directly through model web perception. Do not scrape the webpage. Use IQAir's official API only if a user-provided API key is configured outside the repository.
same_day_environment_context.decision_role: Fresh direct coaching context before weather- or haze-sensitive outdoor calls; do not persist it as a stack state, infer a trend, or let software automatically substitute the session.
fields_of_interest: current weather and rain or thunderstorm context
PM2.5 value, unit and observation time
same_day_environment_context.guardrail: Keep AQI and PM2.5 concentration distinct. Combine the report with current symptoms, trail conditions, expected duration and ventilation; it cannot promote readiness or establish indoor air quality.
same_day_environment_context.location: Taman Tun Dr. Ismail / Bukit Kiara
same_day_environment_context.purpose: Use current weather and displayed air-quality context before a weather- or haze-sensitive outdoor call without making it a persistent stack subsystem.

acute_short_sleep_field_gate.admission: Use only for an isolated 5-to-under-6-hour night with no brain fog, illness, coordination complaint, recent neural-density warning, or adverse HRV/RHR pattern.
acute_short_sleep_field_gate.fail_action: Downshift to low-consequence recovery or end the session for narrowed vision, delayed line choice, reactive braking, unexpected foot or steering correction, repeated line miss, weak feel, or disproportionate RPE.
acute_short_sleep_field_gate.opening_dose: Begin with 10-15 minutes of easy movement plus one familiar low-consequence skill segment; this is an execution test, not automatic clearance.
acute_short_sleep_field_gate.pass_action: Permit one bounded familiar moderate-consequence submaximal dose inside the written contract; do not promote to maximum speed, novelty, jumps, race simulation, or setup testing.
pass_markers: Normal visual scanning and decision speed.
Consistent braking markers and deliberate release.
Early familiar line choice with normal bike-body separation.
No unforced correction, RPE mismatch, or coordination error.

sleep_work_timing_governor.current_context: Clayton's AI workflow for NYSE and Nasdaq trading often extends late into the Kuala Lumpur evening. Train after the main sleep period and before the next market-work window; exact recurring work hours still require prospective logging.
sleep_work_timing_governor.decision_role: Keep primary sleep opportunity, completed nap evidence, late cognitive-work exposure, and autonomic recovery separate. Sleep duration constrains the call independently even when Garmin sleep score, HRV, or Body Battery look good.
evidence_order: Primary sleep start, end, duration, and rolling short-sleep density.
Actual prior work-end time, cognitive-work strain, late caffeine, and whether work crossed midnight.
Completed nap or sleep-extension timing, duration, sleep inertia, and post-nap mental clarity.
Fresh physical readiness, CNS processing, Garmin autonomic context, and recent training density.
non_compensation_rules: A good Garmin sleep score does not cancel a short primary sleep duration.
A Body Battery recharge later in the day is intraday recovery evidence; it must not be rewritten as the wake or morning anchor.
A planned nap is not evidence until completed and reported; a completed nap does not erase chronic short-sleep density.
Low average stress early in the day is partial pre-work evidence, not proof that the demanding workday was controlled.
A late endpoint cutoff does not make daily stress representative when the internal series contains a material wearable gap.
placement_rules: Preserve a late-afternoon pre-market window for recoverable Suito work when it fits Clayton's actual schedule.
Place key MTB late morning or early afternoon after the best sleep opportunity and after sleep inertia has cleared.
Do not add hard post-20:00 training without prospective evidence that it preserves sleep and next-day response.
If work timing prevents two protected MTB opportunities, use the minimum viable week: one controlled Suito session and one MTB session.

provisional_gates.primary_sleep_5_to_under_6h: Treat an isolated night as acute short-sleep amber, not automatic CNS compromise. When current clarity and coordination are normal, illness is absent, autonomic context is stable, rolling sleep and recent neural density are acceptable, and a consequence-sensitive field gate is clean, permit controlled indoor work or familiar capped MTB. Do not permit maximum speed, jumps, novel/high-consequence lines, race simulation, setup testing, or stacked variables.
provisional_gates.primary_sleep_at_least_6_5h: Normal session eligibility only when current physical readiness, CNS processing, density, route consequence, and the session contract also agree.
provisional_gates.primary_sleep_under_5h: Recovery only when accompanied by brain fog, delayed processing, poor coordination, or other red evidence; otherwise no speed, jumps, setup testing, maximal standing efforts, or high-consequence descending.
provisional_gates.rolling_7d_under_6h: Cap the week at two meaningful-cost sessions; a third bike touch must be easy and optional MTB or lower-body gym density is removed first.
provisional_gates.two_consecutive_nights_under_6h: Postpone or convert the next high-consequence session unless the head coach documents why fresh subjective/CNS evidence safely changes the call.

hard_guards: A positive Garmin nap label may support occurrence; zero, empty, or missing Garmin nap data never disproves an athlete-confirmed nap.
Body Battery alone cannot classify a window as restorative and cannot promote high-consequence training.

Even a restorative result cannot raise physical readiness, the CNS ceiling, the technical ceiling, or the written session, and cannot erase primary-sleep, illness, freshness, density, Sabbath, or consequence constraints.
Poor post-rest clarity, prolonged inertia, and active or suspected illness may lower the CNS ceiling but positive rest evidence has no upward path.
Wrong-date outer or nested all-day data cannot satisfy a current rest window; latest failed/empty refresh state remains visible while the last nonempty target-date raw response is preserved.
joined_evidence: Athlete-confirmed local start/end and estimated sleep or rest duration.
Descriptor-aware pre/during/post all-day stress with negative Garmin sentinels excluded from numeric summaries.
Paired near-boundary Body Battery response and recharge-onset latency without replacing the canonical wake/current readiness anchors.
Primary-sleep shortfall and a seven-day observed sleep-opportunity shortfall proxy, explicitly not clinical sleep debt.
Structured illness status, exact or elapsed-duration-derived preceding 48-hour training load, sleep inertia, and post-window clarity.

sleep_work_timing_governor.validation: Run a 2-3 week prospective segmented-sleep/work-timing audit before treating naps or a fixed clock-time schedule as Clayton-specific architecture.

hard_guards: Missing or negative-sentinel samples never prove off-wrist status without athlete confirmation.
A direct wrist-HR gap confirms optical-HR measurement unavailability only; it cannot prove physical watch removal or assign dress-watch use, loose fit, showering, charging, or another cause.
A stress-only unavailable run with continuing wrist HR is not an optical-contact gap; retain it as stress-specific unavailability with unknown mechanism.
Keep measurement availability, physical wear state, and cause attribution as separate axes for every material run.
A recurring Sunday dress-watch habit cannot instantiate a dated window or exact timing.
Attribute every material run independently; an exact dated report explains only its overlap, and unmatched run time remains unexplained.
Wear-state context cannot convert a failed, empty, wrong-date, or retained endpoint attempt into success.
Never impute stress, Body Battery, sleep, HRV, steps, source cutoffs, or readiness across a wearable gap.
Material internal unavailability withholds positive low-stress credit in CNS and predictive models; high observed stress may still downshift.
Positive low-stress use requires dense target-date valid samples from near midnight through a declared cutoff at or after 18:00, with credible Garmin cadence and no uncovered tail.
Fresh target-date wear coverage supersedes any cached same-day model prediction that depended on low stress; mask it until rebuilt rather than letting a date-only cache preserve optimism.
Wear-state evidence cannot raise physical readiness, CNS readiness, technical consequence, or the written session.
inputs: Descriptor-aware all-day stress timestamps, valid values, negative sentinels, and missing timestamp slots.
Body Battery measured/missing status and reset boundaries, without bridging a delta across missing wear.
Direct target-date Fenix wrist-HR samples and timestamp gaps from get_heart_rates, interpreted only as optical-HR measurement availability at sample-transition resolution.
Strict target-date athlete-confirmed off-wrist start/end windows using bounded reason categories.
Recurring wearable habits as context only; exact dated occurrence and timing are never instantiated from a usual pattern.
Endpoint success, latest-attempt state, last success, and retained-response provenance kept separate from series coverage.

directive_macro_coach: Give each day and each ride a specific job.
Protect non-negotiables: bike continuity, two MTB exposures when possible, Sunday rest, and trail quality.
Use stop rules when technique, braking, arm durability, or focus degrades.
garmin_digital_twin_coach: Verify readiness, CNS readiness, training status, devices, gear, self-evaluation, and recent load before prescribing.
Store a pre-session expected result and compare it with actual load, RPE, feel, and next-day wellness.
Classify execution drift before calling a model miss or adaptation problem.
Keep nominal-contract validation separate from delivered-action response, execution-boundary learning, and safety-adherence learning.
Use subjective trail notes to train what Garmin cannot see.

anti_patterns: Spawning agents for vague brainstorming without a concrete deliverable.
Letting a subagent prescribe training without current readiness evidence.
Duplicating the same investigation across agents.
Allowing model novelty to outrank simple validated coaching rules.
subagent_delegation_model.authorization: Clayton has authorized bounded subagent delegation; the main assistant remains head coach, lead engineer, and final decision owner.
governance: Use subagents only for concrete, bounded work that materially improves the coaching or stack outcome.
Subagents may advise or implement scoped changes, but the main assistant owns final training prescriptions, code integration, and Git hygiene.
No subagent output can override fresh readiness evidence, Sunday Sabbath, CNS readiness, data-quality caveats, or the schema v3 session contract.
Subagent advice must state assumptions, confidence, evidence used, and what would change the recommendation.

roles.ai_prediction_researcher: Tests action/state prediction, backtests, baseline comparisons, and whether model output should influence coaching.
roles.coaching_physiology: Reviews load, adaptation, FTP/VO2, fatigue, readiness, CNS status, density, and week structure.
roles.garmin_data_engineer: Maintains sync, artifact hygiene, lap parsing, gear/device audits, and fast same-day decision paths.
roles.mtb_skills_and_setup: Reviews braking, body position, line choice, bike-body separation, suspension feel, clipless adaptation, jumps, and descending quality.
roles.nutrition_heat: Reviews carbs, sodium, hydration, recovery, and Kuala Lumpur heat effects on technical execution.
roles.qa_git_steward: Checks tests, dirty worktree risk, GitHub backup, raw-data protection, and documentation alignment.

use_cases: Parallel code review or implementation on disjoint file scopes.
Independent MTB setup interpretation when subjective trail notes are technically nuanced.
Model validity review before promoting a predictor into coaching decisions.
Data hygiene audit when sync, artifact freshness, or Garmin metadata becomes noisy.

technical_interpretation_standard.clipless_body_position_frame: Do not reduce clipless gains to 'riding more forward.' The expert interpretation is that clipless can provide enough foot security for Clayton to remain dynamically centred, maintain front-tyre authority, and use a larger range of bike-body separation.
technical_interpretation_standard.equipment_causality_rule: Treat suspension and cockpit setup changes as secondary consequences of changed rider loading, speed, terrain, and confidence; do not generalize them into universal clipless setup rules.
response_shape: Identify the primary rider adaptation before the equipment implication.
Name the technical mechanism in expert MTB terms.
Prescribe the next constraint or test.
setup_validation_criteria: Keep a fork rebound change only if the fork does not pack down under repeated hits.
Keep a shock rebound change only if the rear does not kick or wallow through repeated compressions.
Keep the combined chassis setting only if the bike recovers without pitching entering and exiting steep chutes or linked corners.
technical_interpretation_standard.voice: Direct, diagnostic, specific, and willing to sharpen Clayton's interpretation rather than merely agree with it.

after_mtb: braking timing compared with first descent
final descent quality compared with first descent
logging_contract.why: Garmin sees engine and load; it does not see expert-skill execution.

macrocycle.exit_gate: Three consecutive weeks near 5-6 bike touches when logistics allow, with 2-3 low-cost touches, at least 2 MTB exposures, no density breach, no poor next-morning response, and no trail-skill collapse late in rides.
key_sessions: Indoor tempo/torque: 3x8 progressing to 3x12 before raising power.
MTB quality: low-to-moderate volume, high focus on braking, line choice, and corner exits.
MTB durability: repeat climbs/descents while preserving final-descent quality.
macrocycle.purpose: Restore repeatable bike-specific weekly rhythm without reintroducing a load spike.

macrocycle.exit_gate: Can complete a practice-style trail day and feel capable of attacking the next bike day after normal recovery.
key_sessions: Quality trail day: braking/cornering/line choice with full-focus reps.
Durability trail day: 3-5 repeat climbs and descents, fuelled.
Indoor bike: tempo/threshold durability or short repeatability, not both in the same overloaded week.
macrocycle.purpose: Turn rebuilt bike continuity into Bukit Kiara enduro repeatability.

macrocycle.exit_gate: Power and trail handling improve together without needing non-bike load to prop up total training volume.
key_sessions: Optional clean P20/FTP validation when readiness and bike continuity are stable; do not erase the current Garmin operational FTP while waiting.
Repeat 2-5 min punch work for stage surges and climb attacks.
Race-format simulations with controlled Saturday/Sunday proxy around Sabbath constraints.
macrocycle.purpose: Layer threshold, VO2, and 2-5 min repeat power on top of trail durability.

macrocycle.exit_gate: The final run of the day is technically assertive, not merely survived.
key_sessions: PCP jump/scrub timing and landing tolerance.
Wet-tech braking and line choice sessions when conditions allow.
Enduro stage repeatability with fuelling and heat strategy.
macrocycle.purpose: Train aggressive technical execution: jumps, drops, slides, heavy braking, and speed under fatigue.

mission.north_star_metric: Can Clayton ride the final descent of the day with the same aggression, braking precision, and corner-exit speed as the first one?
mission.performance_goal: Build the physical and technical ability to absorb a chill Saturday practice day and still attack Sunday-style race efforts.
mission.primary: Coach Clayton from experienced MTB rider toward expert enduro MTB performance using Garmin evidence, subjective trail notes, and coaching judgment.

matched_route_repeat_load_prior.activation: Opt in only through an explicit versioned session.action_identity; never infer a named route from prose or GPS shape.
matched_route_repeat_load_prior.role: Load-expectation prior only; it is separate from physiology and full digital-twin calibration eligibility.
sample_rules: Use only activity-scoped structured feedback recorded before the prediction date.
Require corroborating Garmin Gear, external-HR provenance, dated loop structure, official-load agreement, comparable duration, and independent activity dates.
Fewer than two comparable samples fails closed; retain the generic estimate for audit but do not simulate it as the matched action.
Keep the immutable dated prediction unchanged; a later route-repeat prior updates future prescriptions only.

post_session: After Garmin sync, compare actual load, self-evaluation, and next-day response with the stored expectation.
If actual load differs materially, classify execution/adherence before judging adaptation.

Keep four learning lanes explicit: nominal-contract validation, delivered-action response, execution-boundary learning, and safety-adherence learning. Do not collapse a session to one eligible/ineligible label.

Only complete contract-quality sessions are eligible for nominal-contract validation: matched load, modality/session-count/duration alignment, explicit stop-rule outcome, complete relevant review fields, clean technical outcome when applicable, and next-day Garmin response.

A triggered-but-continued stop rule permanently excludes nominal-contract validation, but structured rep/lap evidence may still characterize the execution boundary immediately, the stop override may update safety-adherence learning, and a matched next-day response may later enter the delivered-action lane at reduced out-of-policy weight.
Never treat favorable next-day recovery after a stop-rule override as proof that violating the rule was safe, and never claim the unobserved rule-compliant counterfactual response.

Audit raw timing, elevation, moving/rest, device temperature, Garmin estimated water loss, power, Training Effect/TSS, Gear, HR-source confidence, matching loop context, fueling rates, and session/next-day CNS when available; these improve interpretation but cannot loosen calibration eligibility.
If actual load matches but response misses, treat the miss as a model-calibration signal and inspect heat, fueling, sleep, stress, trail violence, and sensor quality.
If load matches but trail skill faded, treat the workout as under-fuelled, under-recovered, too technically dense, or poorly targeted until notes prove otherwise.
If CNS readiness misses the plan, update the technical-consequence gate before changing the physical load model.
pre_session: Store expected duration, training load, high-intensity minutes, RPE range, and next-day response before training.
Store the adaptation hypothesis and the execution stop rules so the review can judge quality, not only load.
Store the expected CNS and technical sharpness state for MTB sessions when recent stress, illness, or brain fog is part of the decision.
Store an execution-drift stress test when similar Clayton prescriptions historically became longer or harder than written.

Record separate state-basis, action, and next-day response dates; if target-day wellness is absent, use the prior wellness row only as an explicitly labelled state basis while simulating the action on its planned date.
Use the coaching-adjusted strain response for the practical call while keeping the raw tree output visible for audit.
Mark model confidence from validation; experimental predictions can guide questions but should not govern training automatically.
predictive_training_loop.purpose: Turn each prescription into a testable expectation for Clayton's digital twin.

progression_rules: Progress only one lever at a time: ride count, MTB technical consequence, duration, intensity, or gym load.
A week with fewer than 2 bike touches is a maintenance failure for MTB goals unless there is a clear logistical reason.
The active build target is 5-6 unique bike days, but missed sleep, work, church/family logistics, or a hard run may reduce the count; never game frequency with doubles or hidden intensity.
A week with high total load but low bike load is not a build week for enduro.
After two MTB days close together, use next-morning feel and upper-body durability response before adding intensity.
Use deloads by cutting non-essential load first, then intensity, while preserving at least easy bike touch when possible.
If sleep is under 5.5 hours and HRV is unbalanced, remove intensity and keep only skill, Z2, recovery, or rest.
Evaluate primary sleep duration independently from Garmin sleep score, HRV, and Body Battery; autonomic green does not make sleep opportunity complete.
If primary sleep is under 5 hours, remove high-consequence technical work and maximal intensity; use recovery when mental clarity, coordination, or CNS evidence is also impaired.

If an isolated primary sleep is 5 to under 6 hours, use acute short-sleep amber: controlled familiar training requires normal current cognition and coordination, stable supporting context, low recent neural density, and a clean consequence-sensitive field gate; never auto-promote to maximum speed, jumps, novelty, race simulation, setup testing, or stacked variables.
If rolling 7-day primary sleep remains under 6 hours, allow at most two meaningful-cost sessions and make the third bike touch easy.
If legs feel good but arms/grip are dead, skip jumps and high-speed DH; use braking/cornering control or recover.
If CNS readiness is impaired or compromised, remove technical consequence even when legs, motivation, or Body Battery look acceptable.
If CNS is watch-level, use one familiar skill target and stop when decision speed or vision narrows.
If Body Battery wakes low and key trail days are ahead, cut indoor intensity before cutting the protected trail day.
Historical finger injury is retained as context only; it must not gate current riding unless Clayton reports a new symptom.

session_contract.adaptation_hypothesis: State what should improve and what next-day response would mean the dose was absorbed.
session_contract.dose: Specify duration, repeats, descents/stages, load cap, RPE/HR/power cap where useful, and what makes the session complete.
session_contract.execution_rules: Describe how to ride the session and what not to chase.
session_contract.expected_result: Store expected Garmin load/range, high-intensity minutes, RPE/feel, and next-day readiness expectation before training when the predictive loop is used.
session_contract.post_session_review: Record the required review fields after the session. For nominal-contract validation, record an explicit stop_rule_outcome. MTB/technical work must also record technical_quality_notes and late_session_skill_fade; a triggered-but-continued stop rule permanently rejects nominal validation, while still permitting separately labelled execution-boundary, safety-adherence, and later delivered-action learning when the evidence is adequate.
session_contract.purpose: Every prescription must state exactly what adaptation it is buying: continuity, torque/threshold, repeatability, braking durability, fork setup, jump timing, wet-tech confidence, or recovery.
stop_rules: End technical work if braking timing gets lazy or line choice becomes reactive.
End DH/jump quality if arm pump changes grip, brake modulation, or body position.
End intensity if HR drift or RPE turns a controlled session into survival.
Downshift immediately if rain or wet roots/rocks raise consequence beyond the session purpose.
Stop or move indoors when current environmental conditions or symptoms make the planned outdoor exposure inappropriate.
Downshift technical consequence if brain fog, visual processing, braking timing, or line choice gets slower than the first quality rep.

bukit_dinding_dh_setup.current_enduro_fork_note: For the next Dinding test, compare baseline against 1 click more rebound damping and 1 click less low-speed compression damping on the Zeb Ultimate.
bukit_dinding_dh_setup.execution: Classify access as uplift, self-pedaled, or mixed. For uplift days, prescribe by descent count and quality; for self-pedaled days, also cap climbing load.
bukit_dinding_dh_setup.purpose: Develop DH line confidence, braking durability, arm-pump tolerance, and suspension setup without confusing uplift load with pedaled enduro load.
bukit_dinding_dh_setup.setup_rule: Change only one suspension variable at a time and compare arm pump, brake dive, front grip, harshness, and corner-entry support.

cns_recovery_gate.allowed_work: Rest, easy circulation, mobility, familiar low-speed skill repetition, or short low-consequence bike touch.
cns_recovery_gate.blocked_work: Intervals, speed hunting, high-consequence descents, jump progression, race simulation, heavy gym loading, and stacked bike/setup variables.
cns_recovery_gate.purpose: Return the nervous system to reliable technical processing before speed, jumps, enduro simulation, or setup testing.
cns_recovery_gate.use_when: Brain fog, low HRV, high stress, weak feel at low RPE, delayed line choice, or slow braking decisions are present.

elliptical_recovery.purpose: Recovery, circulation, and aerobic support without replacing bike-specific work.
elliptical_recovery.red_flag: Hard elliptical during a low-bike week hides the problem instead of solving it.

enduro_repeatability_intervals.placement_rule: Use only when it does not blunt the next key MTB exposure; skip it in weeks with Friday/Saturday back-to-back trail focus.
progression: later progress toward 5-6x2 min hard / 3 min easy
enduro_repeatability_intervals.purpose: Train repeated hard efforts after descents and repeated 2-5 min punch without turning every week into VO2 survival.
enduro_repeatability_intervals.starter_dose: 2 sets of 5x30 sec hard / 90 sec easy, 6 min easy between sets.

indoor_steady_endurance.back_to_back_rule: Back-to-back 60-minute low-cost doses are allowed when global RPE remains 2-3, mechanics are stable, the muscular response is diffuse and bilateral, symptoms resolve promptly, and the following protected session is not compromised.
indoor_steady_endurance.duration_development_dose: Progress one weekly exposure through 75 minutes toward 90 minutes near 125 W. Treat it as moderate or meaningful cost until 90 minutes is absorbed with global RPE no higher than 4, controlled mechanics and normal next-day function.
indoor_steady_endurance.high_end_benchmark: Sixty minutes near 145 W is high-end endurance for Clayton and counts as the week's structured engine exposure. Use it every two to four weeks as a benchmark or development session, not in addition to torque or VO2 work.
indoor_steady_endurance.progression_gate: Progress duration after two absorbed standard doses or one clean duration-development confirmation. Do not require an absence of all terminal muscular sensation before training endurance; require stable execution and recovery.
indoor_steady_endurance.purpose: Rebuild the bike-specific mitochondrial, peripheral and seated muscular durability that supported Clayton's strongest continuity blocks without making every bike day costly.
indoor_steady_endurance.routine_low_cost_dose: 60 minutes total with approximately 40 minutes at 120-130 W, global RPE 2-3 and normal ceiling-fan cooling. This is the default continuity dose, not a dose that must be repeatedly shortened merely because another key session exists.
indoor_steady_endurance.symptom_interpretation: A familiar diffuse bilateral glute or hamstring burn limited to the final minutes and resolving to 0/10 is an adaptation marker. Track later onset and lower intensity as progress. Downshift or stop for focal or asymmetric pain, altered pedalling or posture, neurological symptoms, persistence beyond approximately 30 minutes, or next-day functional impairment.

indoor_tempo_torque.cadence_bias: 65-75 rpm unless knee/hip comfort says otherwise.
indoor_tempo_torque.power_guidance: Use the latest dated Garmin operational FTP for relative targets and validate against RPE/HR; do not substitute historical 222 W P20 or treat Garmin estimation as a clean-test guarantee.
progression: raise watts only after repeatability is easy
indoor_tempo_torque.purpose: Rebuild bike force and threshold durability using the current Garmin operational FTP, RPE, and HR without turning every bike touch into intensity.
indoor_tempo_torque.stop_rule: Stop adding work when cadence/form degrades or HR drift makes the final rep survival.

kiara_practice_race_proxy.execution: Climb mostly Z2/tempo, use short controlled surges late in selected climbs, descend smooth and precise, stop when descending quality drops below 7/10.
kiara_practice_race_proxy.fueling_priority: Start carbs in the first 20 min; late braking mistakes and timid riding may be heat or fuel failures.
kiara_practice_race_proxy.purpose: Rebuild the ability to absorb a chill practice-style day and still ride aggressively the next key day.

low_cost_skill.dose: 60-90 min max, full recovery between quality reps, no big sends when tired.
low_cost_skill.purpose: Maintain skill touch without stealing from the next durability or DH day.

mtb_durability_enduro.purpose: Build the ability to keep climbing and descending without losing aggression.
mtb_durability_enduro.quality_rule: The last descent must still be technically sharp.

mtb_quality_skill.example_dose: 6-8 focused reps of one corner, chute, jump timing, or braking-release point; finish with 1-2 smooth descents at controlled pace.
mtb_quality_skill.purpose: Raise expert-skill ceiling while fresh enough to learn.
mtb_quality_skill.volume_rule: Low to moderate volume; end before slop becomes the main thing being rehearsed.

strength_support.interference_rule: Any DOMS or dead legs that reduces Friday/Saturday trail quality means the gym dose was too high or badly placed.
strength_support.purpose: Support braking, descending posture, impact tolerance, and long-run durability.

weekly_architecture.back_to_back_proxy: Use Friday practice-style exposure plus Saturday attack-style effort to train race weekend demands while preserving Sunday Sabbath.

default_week.friday: Indoor low-aerobic continuity at the standard 60-minute dose when Saturday is not already the week's third meaningful cost; use a shorter primer only when fresh evidence shows it protects a specific Saturday objective.
default_week.monday: Preferred conversational run with Clayton's wife. If the run does not happen, use the standard 60-minute low-aerobic bike dose rather than defaulting to rest; if the run happens, count its cost honestly and place the long bike dose elsewhere.
default_week.saturday: Optional third MTB skill-transfer/Enduro-bike exposure; skip for church/family obligations or density.
default_week.thursday: Protected MTB durability or technical-quality exposure.

density_governor: Build toward 5-6 bike touches through 2-3 low-cost Z1/Z2 or primer days; do not manufacture frequency with split files or unnecessary doubles.

The two-touch minimum is an emergency maintenance floor, not a successful build target. A normal trainable week below five unique bike days is underdosed unless a named hard constraint removed the opportunity.

Do not repeatedly protect the next key ride by shrinking ordinary low-cost continuity. Sixty minutes at 120-130 W is Clayton's default low-cost Suito dose when global RPE is 2-3 and there is no persistent or mechanically altering symptom.

Every normal build week needs one explicit progressive-overload target: steady-endurance duration, structured-engine dose, or MTB repeatability. A week made entirely of primers, recovery rides and capped skill sessions is not a fitness-development week.
Keep only 2-3 sessions meaningfully costly, and count a hard run toward that cap.
If Friday and Saturday are both trail days, Thursday becomes primer or recovery, not repeatability intervals.
If a Tuesday or Wednesday MTB ride creates arm pump or high load, remove lower-body strength and indoor intensity until the key trail days are protected.

Use one hard engine session plus one or two trail-specific sessions as the default; do not stack threshold, repeatability, and two hard MTB days in the same rebuild week unless recovery is clearly green.
If CNS readiness is impaired or compromised, protect recovery and low-consequence repetition before protecting weekly load targets.
Protect 2 MTB exposures per week and allow up to 3 when readiness, CNS readiness, logistics, and load density support it; more than 3 is an event/race block, not a default build week.
When in doubt, protect the session that most resembles the goal event demand.
high_return_week: Five bike touches: two protected MTB exposures plus three low-cost/controlled bike touches; a sixth is optional only when recovery and calendar support it.
Only 2-3 sessions across bike and hard running may be meaningfully costly.
One recovery elliptical only if it improves next-day freshness.
minimum_viable_week: Two bike touches: one indoor torque/tempo and one MTB ride.
One short support strength or mobility dose only if it does not reduce bike quality.
No attempt to replace missed bike with hard elliptical and call it equivalent.

schedule_translation.indoor_preference: Use a late-afternoon pre-market slot for controlled Suito work when it leaves adequate transition time for work and does not delay the next primary sleep.
schedule_translation.mtb_preference: Use late morning or early afternoon after the best sleep opportunity, cleared sleep inertia, and a fresh CNS check.
schedule_translation.rule: The weekday template expresses session roles, not immutable clock placement. Resolve actual sessions around sleep opportunity, prior work-end time, planned market-work window, family/church obligations, readiness, and density.

six_week_rebuild_targets.elliptical_or_run: Recovery/support only; never counted as bike-specific maintenance.

mtb_sessions_per_week.ideal: 2-3 with one quality and one durability exposure

strength_sessions_per_week.ideal: 2 small doses only if trail quality is unaffected
